Load/validate source, save definitions with ten
a script, and resolve init bindings. Saving

The simple flow specialization: the same four stages in the same
order, with every stage's exit gated. The first three stages use
fixed checks; verification uses a record check and inherited
semantic judgment. xdesign.designedSimpleFlow is the selectable
One checkpoint of the designed simple flow, abstracted
as one class for both kinds of rule. The class adapts
the flow's syntax rules and its semantic rules: a
syntactic checkpoint binds the checker whose command
fixes the check and the rules that decide it, declared
here and documented in D06; a semantic checkpoint…
The syntactic adaptation of the checkpoint class:
a fixed command applies its declared checker
rules. The declared command must exist and return
a revision-bound report with the exact rule set
before this gate can pass. Its evaluate operation
retains the per-rule report as evidence.
The semantic adaptation of the checkpoint class:
criteria a permitted judge reads, with no
checker. Its evaluate operation presents the
criteria and the visit's artifacts and evidence
to the judge and records the rationale. The
logic a criterion states stays prose for the…
The evaluate operation of a checkpoint class,
for one gate and one visit: read the class's
rules, take the path its adaptation fixes, and
produce one assessment. A syntactic checkpoint's
rules are its checker's CheckerRules, applied by
the command and reported rule by rule; a…

order. Each checkpoint's evaluate operation takes
the path its adaptation fixes. A syntactic

The successor rule of the designed flow, for one
run: when the current visit is authorized —
every exit gate passed and cited at the visited
revision — decide where the run goes. A stage
with a successor hands the run to that stage's
pending visit, which becomes current. The verify…
Explicit rework of a completed terminal visit. A
completed run can reopen its terminal verification stage
only on a recorded rework request. Keep the completed
visit and its assessments immutable, append a new active
visit for that stage at the next visit index with
artifact revision 0, and return the run to active.…
The check command's interface: the independent
SysML wish trace and the executable run-record
snapshot are both named. The checker identity,
frozen plan ID and hash, stage, artifact
revision and artifact-set digest select the
exact fixed rule set and input. The report…
The caller-command interface a syntactic gate is
run through: the run invokes the named checker
with the wish trace, run record, frozen plan,
stage, revision and artifact-set digest, then
validates the returned rule report and verdict.
The judgment interface: the criteria and the
artifacts go out to a permitted judge, the
outcome and its rationale come back. What a
script cannot settle crosses this interface.

The parts a run of the designed flow is automated by, wired by
their interfaces: the factory creates the run, the run invokes a
checker command through the check command interface, and presents
its semantic gates to a judge through the judgment interface.
One run of the designed flow over time, whatever
wish it answers: the run is created, each stage
is entered and its gate assessed in order, and
the terminal stage's completion finishes the run.

Parametric context for a real stage visit. Counting gates rather than assessments prevents duplicate passes from compensating for a missing gate. A stale or failed assessment contributes nothing.
Lifecycle of one run, distinct from the four
engineering stages. The factory activates the
run. A failed, missing or stale gate blocks it;
corrective work resumes the same current visit
at a new artifact revision. Only authorization
of a terminal visit permits completion.…
The requester's goal: progress a wish to an
evidence-backed delivery, inspect its record and
request corrective work when evidence is
behavior, not another external user goal.

Records a stakeholder concern for one declared
documentation view. A concrete viewpoint usage
names its subject view; that view selects native
model elements with expose and locates its
rendered figure with DocFigure. The concern text

The wish-verify flow specialization: the same two
stages in the same order, with every stage's exit
gated. Both gates are semantic — the architecture
states that nothing in this flow's outcome is
established by a fixed check, so the designed flow
declares no checker, and a permitted agent or human…
One checkpoint of the designed wish-verify flow.
Unlike the simple flow's class it needs no syntactic
adaptation: this flow's gates are all judged. The
class owns the evaluate operation and the assessments
